reuse.why: Routes the enable flag and holidays through the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds a shared isHoliday, but the new daily-skip rule and the 'is this a skipped day' predicate are re-written at call sites instead of being part of the shared definition.

duplication.why: The skipped-day predicate exists three times (inside getDateWithSkippedWeekend, as a local isSkippedDay in getNextDate, inline in getDatesInRange) and the daily-skip decision is coded separately in getNextDate and getDatesInRange with different frequency checks.

placement.why: Holiday matching and the move logic sit in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily rule is split between getNextDate and the server handler rather than living in the shared weekend definition.

scope.why: Mostly the requested steps, with an incidental rename of value.schedule to schedule in getNextDate.

maintainability.why: A future change to which days are skipped or to the daily rule must be made in several diverging copies (and getUpcomingDates/schedule-template do not apply the daily rule at all), which is hard to own.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange and packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts getNextDate decide daily weekend/holiday skips with their own isWeekend/isHoliday checks instead of going through getDateWithSkippedWeekend

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts getNextDate local isSkippedDay closure and server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange inline condition re-express the skipped-day predicate already inside getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the daily-skip branch is reshaped differently in each (loop vs return null, frequency.toLowerCase() vs ===)

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained skipWeekend and holidays parameters; the daily-schedule special case was kept outside it in getNextDate and getDatesInRange, which re-implement the skipped-day test
